quiz.q: Which combination is the strongest sign of phishing?
o: Urgency + lookalike domain + request for money or login

quiz.q: You get repeated MFA prompts you did not trigger. Best action?
o: Read the code to IT on the phone
Deny all and report to security

quiz.q: You find a USB drive in the parking lot. You should:
o: Plug it into your work PC
Hand it to security without plugging it in
Plug it into your home PC

quiz.q: Gathering public information about a target before an attack is called:

emails.subject: Maintenance on Saturday 2 AM
emails.body: Systems will be briefly offline. No action needed.
emails.why: Internal domain, no links, no pressure, no request for information.

emails.subject: URGENT: invoice overdue
emails.body: Pay within 1 hour or services stop: http://cloudpay-secure-login.xyz
emails.why: Unfamiliar domain, extreme urgency, link does not match the vendor.

emails.subject: Updated holiday calendar
emails.body: The 2026 holiday list is on the intranet.
emails.why: Legitimate sender, no link or request. Not every email is an attack.

emails.subject: Quick favor
emails.body: I am in a meeting. Buy 5 gift cards and send me the codes. Keep this confidential.
emails.why: Lookalike domain, secrecy, and a gift-card request. Classic CEO fraud.

emails.subject: Your mailbox is 99% full
emails.body: Log in now to avoid losing mail: http://novatech-mail-verify.xyz/login
emails.why: Not the real company domain, fear tactic, and a login link to an outside site.

emails.subject: Lunch and learn on Thursday
emails.body: Join us Thursday at 1 PM in Room 4. No RSVP needed.
emails.why: Internal sender, no link, nothing sensitive requested.

scenarios.title: 📞 Attacker: Phone Pretext
scenarios.text: You call the receptionist pretending to be IT. You need her to help reset the CEO's account. What is your opening line?
scenarios.hint: Use names from your recon, plus authority and urgency.
scenarios.ref: MITRE ATT&CK T1598 Phishing for Information, T1656 Impersonation

opts.t: Hi, I am Raj from IT. We detected a problem on Priya Mehta's account and I must fix it before her 10 AM board meeting.
opts.why: Authority + urgency + a real name from recon makes this convincing.

opts.t: Hello? I am calling about something.
opts.why: Vague, with no pretext and no leverage.

scenarios.title: ☎️ Defender: Vishing Call
scenarios.text: A caller says: 'This is your bank's fraud team. Your account is being drained. Read us the OTP we just sent so we can cancel it.'
scenarios.hint: A real bank never asks for your OTP.

opts.why: The OTP lets the attacker authorize the transfer themselves.

opts.t: Hang up and call the number printed on your bank card.
opts.why: Correct. Always call back on a number you trust.

opts.t: Ask them to tell you your balance first to prove who they are.
opts.why: Attackers may already hold partial data, so this proves nothing.

scenarios.title: 💾 Defender: USB Drop
scenarios.text: In the parking lot you find a USB drive labelled 'Salary 2026 - Confidential'.
scenarios.hint: Curiosity is exactly what the attacker is counting on.
scenarios.ref: MITRE ATT&CK T1091 Replication Through Removable Media

opts.t: Plug it into your work PC to find the owner.
opts.why: It could be a malicious device that runs code as soon as it is connected.

opts.t: Plug it into your home PC instead.
opts.why: Still dangerous, and now your personal data is at risk.

opts.t: Hand it to the security team without plugging it in.

scenarios.title: 🚪 Defender: Tailgating
scenarios.text: A person in a delivery uniform, hands full, asks you to hold the secure door open.
scenarios.hint: Being polite and being secure are not the same thing here.

opts.t: Hold the door. They look legitimate.
opts.why: Uniforms are easy to fake. They bypassed your badge control.

opts.t: Politely ask them to badge in or go to reception.
opts.why: Correct. Politely redirecting is the safe habit.

opts.t: Let them in but keep an eye on them.
opts.why: They are already inside and unverified.

scenarios.title: 📱 Defender: MFA Fatigue
scenarios.text: It is 2 AM. Your phone shows 6 login approval requests you did not make. Then 'IT Support' calls: 'Just approve one so the alerts stop.'
scenarios.hint: Repeated prompts mean someone already has your password.
scenarios.ref: MITRE ATT&CK T1621 MFA Request Generation

opts.t: Approve one to make it stop.
opts.why: This gives the attacker full access.

opts.t: Ignore it and go back to sleep.
opts.why: Better, but security never learns your password is compromised.

opts.t: Deny all and report to the security team.
